headline: Mozaffar shown arrested in crimes against humanity case
summary: The accused, who is also linked to the assassination of Ziaur Rahman, was produced before the International Crimes Tribunal.
details: Mozaffar has been officially shown arrested in a case involving crimes against humanity.
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) processed the arrest of the individual.
According to reports, Mozaffar is an accused in the case concerning the assassination of former President Ziaur Rahman.
The legal proceedings regarding these allegations are now moving forward under the jurisdiction of the ICT.
caption:
A key accused in the assassination of Ziaur Rahman has been shown arrested in a crimes against humanity case.

Mozaffar has been officially shown arrested in a case involving crimes against humanity.

The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) processed the arrest of the individual.

According to reports, Mozaffar is an accused in the case concerning the assassination of former President Ziaur Rahman.

The legal proceedings regarding these allegations are now moving forward under the jurisdiction of the ICT.

headline_marked: 17 high-ranking [[police officers sent into forced retirement]] by government
headline: 17 high-ranking police officers sent into forced retirement by government
summary: The group includes 3 DIGs, 12 Additional DIGs, and 2 SPs, acting under the Government Servants Act 2018.
details: The Bangladesh government has sent 17 high-ranking police officers into forced retirement on Thursday.
Among those retired are 3 Deputy Inspector Generals (DIGs), 12 Additional DIGs, and 2 Superintendents of Police (SPs).
The action was taken in the public interest under Section 45 of the Government Servants Act, 2018.
A notification signed by Senior Secretary of the Public Security Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Manzur Morshed Chowdhury, detailed the decision.
The list of retired officers includes Mohammad Abdullahil Baqi, the DIG of Highway Police.
According to the notification, the retired officers will receive all benefits and allowances as per existing rules.
caption:
17 high-ranking police officers, including 3 DIGs, have been forced into retirement by the government.

The Bangladesh government has sent 17 high-ranking police officers into forced retirement on Thursday.

Among those retired are 3 Deputy Inspector Generals (DIGs), 12 Additional DIGs, and 2 Superintendents of Police (SPs).

The action was taken in the public interest under Section 45 of the Government Servants Act, 2018.

A notification signed by Senior Secretary of the Public Security Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Manzur Morshed Chowdhury, detailed the decision.

The list of retired officers includes Mohammad Abdullahil Baqi, the DIG of Highway Police.

According to the notification, the retired officers will receive all benefits and allowances as per existing rules.
